newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts this week - Set to outperform US Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts this week - Set to outperform US Treasuries.

text.p: UK gilts are set to extend recent gains this week with December retail sales data, expected to be moderate, reinforcing the improved inflation outlook and paving the way for an outperformance of U.S. Treasuries, analysts said.
"On the whole it's going to be a decent week, depending on the U.S. market," said Bank America economist Jeremy Hawkins. "The background is looking more positive than for some time."
Gilts powered ahead at the end of last week after a fall in underlying inflation prompted investors to revise their expectations of an imminent rise in UK interest rates.

Key retail sales data due on Wednesday are seen reinforcing these expectations. According to a Reuter poll, economists expect retail sales to rise 0.1 percent in December, down from November's heady 0.7 percent jump. Annual growth is seen slowing to 3.5 percent in December from 3.9 percent the previous month.
Tom Rayner, gilts analyst at Societe Generale, said the retail sales data, and Tuesday's December M4 money supply data, would do little to restrain the market's positive sentiment.
"The improved outlook on inflation has prompted some large switching from Bunds into gilts," he said.
"We believe that further tightening can occur, with the technical picture suggesting that there is greater room for gilts to rally than for Bunds."
The 10-year gilt/Bund spread was at 176 basis points in early Monday trade, down from around 190 basis points just last Wednesday.
Hawkins agreed the spread could narrow further this week.
"In terms of spreads perhaps the gilt/Bund spread could trade down towards the 170 area," he said.
But BZW's Kevin Adams was more cautious.

"There's no clear case for a significant narrowing from here," he said. "But there is a considerable interest in the UK from overseas investors so the sheer weight of money coming in could prompt spread narrowing."

Adams warned Tuesday's quarterly CBI industrial trends survey may upset the market. "Undoubtedly the export side will have been dented by the stronger currency. But looking at the domestic side...expectations could be reasonably buoyant...which could give the market pause for thought."
Adams was more optimistic about gilts' performance versus Treasuries, which may tumble on Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony to the Senate's budget committee on Tuesday.
"The prospect of a need to raise U.S. rates could see Treasuries suffering a bit, so I expect a degree of outperformance," he said.
Analysts said the rally at the long end of the curve was likely to continue, prompting some curve flattening.

"The short end in the UK is probably going to go nowhere in a hurry now. On the assumption we see the U.S. market drifting lower...I see scope for sufficient outperformance by gilts and to see some curve flattening, but not a huge amount," said Hawkins.
